GameEvent.eGameEvent members: player_apply_medikit, player_apply_ammokit, player_apply_disinfection, player_apply_toolRefill
capabilities.publishRule: One fact per posted supply event, carrying the player the event named and the vocabulary member the event maps to. The event is the game's own announcement; nothing is inferred from item state.

ports.player: EntityReference of the player the event named (required)
ports.kind: a string port carrying the member name verbatim: medikit | ammokit | disinfection | tool_refill. A string and not an enum because an enum port must resolve against the framework's one shared enum-set table, which does not carry this set; a member outside the list is refused by name instead of passed through.

capabilities.publishRule: One fact per posted pickup event. The row is the player-side reading of a pickup — who picked up which kind of item — and not the equipment-side `forge.trigger.equipment.picked_up` row, whose subject is the item life; both may be needed and neither is restated by the other.

ports.player: EntityReference of the player the event named (required)
ports.kind: medikit | ammokit | tool_refill | artifact | commodity_small | commodity_medium | commodity_large | consumable | keycard (string port, see the supply row)

notMapped: player_pickup_* events that name a type outside the row's vocabulary are refused by name, never published as an unknown member

capabilities.status: implemented with one open channel (see hostClientVisibility)
hooks: GameEvent.GameEventManager.PostEvent(...) with e == eGameEvent.player_ping; the position is the pinging agent's own Player.LocalPlayerAgent.m_pingPos (UnityEngine.Vector3)

GuiManager.AttemptSetPlayerPingStatus(Player.PlayerAgent sourceAgent, System.Boolean visible, UnityEngine.Vector3 worldPos, eNavMarkerStyle style) (public static, prefix; the same body hides a marker again, so only the visible edge is a ping)
capabilities.publishRule: Two entries are observed because the game reaches two different ones for one ping: the local event names the player without a position, and the marker call names the player and the world position. The half de-duplicates them per life, per tick and per position, so a machine that sees both publishes one fact. A position that is not finite publishes nothing.

ports.position: the world position the ping named, in metres (required)
ports.target: NOT IMPLEMENTED: an entity for the pinged object. PlayerAgent.TriggerMarkerPing(iPlayerPingTarget target, UnityEngine.GameObject targetGameObject, UnityEngine.Vector3 worldPos) does carry the pinged object, but resolving it needs the kernel's object-to-entity entry for the pinged object's own kind, and this half cannot name that kind from a `GameObject`. The port stays declared and optional and is left out of every payload rather than filled with a guess.

capabilities.hostClientVisibility: A ping is produced on the machine of the player who pinged it. `PostEvent` is therefore read where the input happened, and only the authority publishes: a host's own ping is published directly. Whether a client's ping reaches the host through the game's own marker replication (GuiManager holds SyncedNavMarkerWrapper instances, which is what suggests it might) is NOT established by this build's metadata. If a two-machine check shows it does not, the honest fix is a command-request user for this row — the framework has no consumer for a domain package to register yet, which is the missing piece recorded in the report.

sharedRules: Supply and pickup announcements are host-observed events: the host publishes, a client's local event is dropped and reported once per reason.
Every fact id is fact + world epoch + life + per-life transition number; the kernel's ledger answers a repeated id with `duplicate`.
limits: No game run. The open items for this family are the client-ping channel above and whether a client's pickup/supply announcement is observable on the host at all (the game may announce it only on the machine that performed it).
